# Target release

**Target**: CASE/UCO 1.5.0

# Background

`uco-observable:UNIXAccountFacet` currently carries `gid` and `shell` but not the account's numeric user identifier (uid) — the primary key by which UNIX-family operating systems (Linux, macOS, iOS, Android) attribute activity to accounts in logs, file ownership, and process credentials. Similarly, `uco-observable:UNIXProcessFacet` carries `ruid` (real user id) but not `euid` (effective user id), which is the identifier that governs the privilege actually exercised by a process and the one most commonly emitted in modern OS telemetry: Apple Unified Logging rows expose an `euid` column in parser outputs (e.g., Lionel Notari's Unified Logs tooling), and setuid escalation is only visible when both ruid and euid can be asserted. Without these properties, examiners must push core attribution and privilege-escalation evidence into free-text or dictionary entries where it cannot be queried, compared, or validated. Both additions are additive, backward-compatible integer data properties on existing facets.

Semantics are grounded in POSIX getuid(2)/geteuid(2) (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/getuid.2.html, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/geteuid.2.html) and credentials(7) (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/credentials.7.html).

# Requirements

## Requirement 1

Add property `uid` (xsd:nonNegativeInteger) to `uco-observable:UNIXAccountFacet`. The numeric user identifier (UID) of the UNIX account as recorded in the account database (e.g., /etc/passwd, Open Directory). The datatype matches the existing `uco-observable:ruid` convention.

## Requirement 2

Add property `euid` (xsd:nonNegativeInteger) to `uco-observable:UNIXProcessFacet`. The effective user identifier (EUID) of the process, which determines the privilege exercised for access-control decisions; differs from `ruid` when setuid or credential-changing calls have occurred.

# Risk / Benefit analysis

## Benefits

- Account attribution by numeric uid becomes typed and queryable — the key emitted by UNIX-family logs, file ownership metadata, and process credentials.
- The ruid/euid pair makes setuid privilege changes (euid ≠ ruid) directly queryable, core evidence in intrusion and malware investigations.
- Both properties are additive on existing facets; fully backward-compatible.

## Risks

- `uid` on `UNIXAccountFacet` and `ruid`/`euid` on `UNIXProcessFacet` could be conflated by tool authors; property comments should state that account uid characterizes the account database entry while ruid/euid characterize per-process credentials.
- The existing `gid` property uses `xsd:integer` while `ruid` uses `xsd:nonNegativeInteger`; this proposal follows the `ruid` convention, perpetuating a minor inconsistency the committee may wish to harmonize separately.

# Competencies demonstrated

## Competency 1

An examiner reviews Apple Unified Logging output from an iOS 17.3 sysdiagnose parsed with Notari Unified Logs v2. Log rows from locationd run with euid 205 (`_locationd`), while rows from wifid run with euid 0 (root). The examiner needs to model the `_locationd` account with its numeric uid 205 on `UNIXAccountFacet`, and each emitting process with both `ruid` and `euid` on `UNIXProcessFacet`, so that a SPARQL query can (1) attribute log activity to accounts by uid and (2) flag processes whose euid differs from their ruid (setuid privilege change) — evidence that is central to intrusion and malware investigations on any UNIX-family system.

### Competency Question 1.1

Which UNIX account has numeric uid 205 (attributing unified-log activity reported by the euid column to a named account)?

#### Result 1.1

The `_locationd` account observable, selected by typed integer uid.

### Competency Question 1.2

Which processes exhibit a setuid privilege change (effective uid differs from real uid)?

#### Result 1.2

The `suspicious-helper` process (ruid 501, euid 0); the locationd process (ruid = euid = 205) is correctly excluded.

### Draft SPARQL

```sparql
PREFIX uco-observable: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/observable/>
PREFIX uco-core: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/core/>
PREFIX proposed: <http://example.org/ontology/proposed/>

SELECT ?process ?name ?ruid ?euid
WHERE {
    ?process uco-core:name ?name ;
             uco-core:hasFacet ?facet .
    ?facet a uco-observable:UNIXProcessFacet ;
           uco-observable:ruid ?ruid ;
           proposed:euid ?euid .
    FILTER (?euid != ?ruid)
}
```

(The account-attribution query for CQ 1.1 is in `change_proposals/unix-numeric-user-identifier-properties.sparql`.)

I am fine with my examples being transcribed and credited.

# Solution suggestion

* Add property `uid` (`xsd:nonNegativeInteger`) to `uco-observable:UNIXAccountFacet`
* Add property `euid` (`xsd:nonNegativeInteger`) to `uco-observable:UNIXProcessFacet`
* Update SHACL shapes for both facets with the new property constraints
* Add unit test(s) demonstrating valid and invalid usage

A prototype extension ontology used for pre-submission validation is at `change_proposals/unix-numeric-user-identifier-properties.ttl`.
